title: Middleware route information: partial capabilities without resolving the global APM need

boundary_decision.rationale: Issue 685 and PRs 1286, 1649, and 2349 repeatedly address where route-aware middleware can run. The later PRs add partial per-Mount or per-Route capabilities, while timestamped comments preserve the original low-touch global APM need and explain why the issue is reopened rather than resolved.
boundary_decision.falsification: Split the case if an audited source shows that the per-route and per-Mount work was unrelated to exposing routing information to middleware, or that issue 685 was finally resolved before the registered cutoff.

excluded_sources.reason: The body was edited after the premature close and now contains struck-through closure text, so it is not a safe timestamped explanation of the close.
The canary preserves the later timestamped review that records this branch as rejected; expanding the full PR would create a second design branch without changing the registered continuity question.
The mark-scope plus centralized-I/O idea is already established by the earlier immutable PR 1649 comment; this repetition adds no new increment.

The current mutable body says it does not solve issue 685, but its edit time is unavailable. The creation event uses only the creation-time title; final limitations rely on the issue's open state and merge anchor.

source_body_history_limitations: Issue and PR bodies are mutable. Creation events use only creation-time titles verified from GitHub metadata/timeline or an immutable initial commit. Stable comments and reviews use their own timestamps and observed body hashes. State-event hashes cover a documented canonical subset of the GitHub event response.
